summary: TLS everywhere and signed request tokens for all Edge↔Relay traffic (AUTH-FR-04, SP-01): every outbound Edge request is HMAC-SHA256-signed over a canonical request form (method, path, raw query, RFC3339 timestamp, nonce, gateway id) with a purpose-separated key derived from the gateway's registration token; the Relay derives and stores that key at token issue/rotate time (never the token, SP-07) and verifies every /sync/* request, rejecting unsigned requests (401 SIGNATURE_INVALID), unknown identities (404), non-REGISTERED identities (403), stale timestamps, and tampered/rebound requests. TLS is enforced at the Edge (Relay base URL must be https unless an explicit dev opt-in) and at the Relay (HSTS + HTTPS redirection outside Development).

payload.agentOutputExcerpt: TLS everywhere and signed request tokens for Edge↔Relay traffic (AUTH-FR-04, SP-01). The Edge signs every outbound request with an HMAC-SHA256 key derived from its current registration token (purpose label 'humangateway:request-signing:v1'); the Relay derives the same key at token issue/rotate time and stores only that derived key (never the plaintext token, SP-07). GatewayRequestSigningMiddleware verifies every /sync/* request: unknown identities 404, non-REGISTERED 403, missing/stale/invalid signatures 401 SIGNATURE_INVALID, and query/body gateway ids that disagree with the verified identity are rejected. TLS is enforced at the Edge (RelayTlsPolicy.RequireAllowed — https only, loopback/dev opt-in) and the Relay (HSTS + HTTPS redirection outside Development).
